title: Blossoms Twice
setting: A Sunday in early March at the family home. Yuki, who lives on her own, has dropped by and asks her little brother Kenji, who finishes high school this month, about the university in Hokkaido he starts at in April.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, hokkaidou no daigaku ni hairu n da tte? nande hokkaidou ni shita no?
lines.ja: ケンジ、北海道の大学に入るんだって？なんで北海道にしたの？
lines.kana: けんじ、ほっかいどうのだいがくにはいるんだって？なんでほっかいどうにしたの？
lines.english: Kenji, I hear you're going to university in Hokkaido? Why Hokkaido?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atsusa ni yowai kara. kotchi no natsu, mou muri.
lines.ja: 暑さに弱いから。こっちの夏、もう無理。
lines.kana: あつさによわいから。こっちのなつ、もうむり。
lines.english: 'Cause I can't take the heat. I'm done with summers here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sore dake? maa, kenji wa mukashi kara atsusa ni yowai kedo.
lines.ja: え、それだけ？まあ、ケンジは昔から暑さに弱いけど。
lines.kana: え、それだけ？まあ、けんじはむかしからあつさによわいけど。
lines.english: What, that's it? I mean, you've always been hopeless in the heat, but still.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. nanimo shinakute mo ase kaku shi.
lines.ja: 朝からセミが鳴いて、寝られないし。何もしなくても汗かくし。
lines.kana: あさからせみがないて、ねられないし。なにもしなくてもあせかくし。
lines.english: The cicadas start up first thing, so I can't sleep. And I sweat even doing nothing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ee, semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji de ii jan.
lines.ja: えー、セミが鳴くと、夏って感じでいいじゃん。
lines.kana: えー、せみがなくと、なつってかんじでいいじゃん。
lines.english: Aw, but when the cicadas start, it really feels like summer. I like that.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atchi wa, semi anmari nakanai rashii yo. natsu mo sonna ni atsukunai tte.
lines.ja: あっちは、セミあんまり鳴かないらしいよ。夏もそんなに暑くないって。
lines.kana: あっちは、せみあんまりなかないらしいよ。なつもそんなにあつくないって。
lines.english: Apparently the cicadas don't go much up there. And summer's not that hot either.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo, fuyu wa? atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo.
lines.ja: でも、冬は？あっち、雪すごく積もるよ。
lines.kana: でも、ふゆは？あっち、ゆきすごくつもるよ。
lines.english: But what about winter? The snow really piles up there.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shitteru. yuki ga tsumoru no, chotto tanoshimi.
lines.ja: 知ってる。雪が積もるの、ちょっと楽しみ。
lines.kana: しってる。ゆきがつもるの、ちょっとたのしみ。
lines.english: I know. I'm kind of looking forward to the snow piling up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yuki wa futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo.
lines.ja: 雪は降ってるだけならきれいだけど、積もると大変だよ。
lines.kana: ゆきはふってるだけならきれいだけど、つもるとたいへんだよ。
lines.english: Snow's pretty while it's coming down, but once it settles, it's a real pain.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: daijoubu. atsusa ni wa yowai kedo, samusa ni wa yowakunai kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。暑さには弱いけど、寒さには弱くないから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。あつさにはよわいけど、さむさにはよわくないから。
lines.english: I'll be fine. I can't take the heat, but I'm OK with the cold.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uso. fuyu wa itsumo, samui samui tte, asa okirenai jan.
lines.ja: うそ。冬はいつも、寒い寒いって、朝起きれないじゃん。
lines.kana: うそ。ふゆはいつも、さむいさむいって、あさおきれないじゃん。
lines.english: Liar. Every winter you go 'it's freezing, it's freezing' and can't get out of bed.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore to kore to wa betsu.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. a, sou ieba, atchi tte sakura ga saku no, osoi n da yo ne?
lines.ja: はいはい。あ、そういえば、あっちって桜が咲くの、遅いんだよね？
lines.kana: はいはい。あ、そういえば、あっちってさくらがさくの、おそいんだよね？
lines.english: Sure, sure. Oh, come to think of it, the cherry blossoms come out late up there, don't they?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. netto de shirabetara, kotchi yori ikkagetsu gurai osoku saku tte.
lines.ja: うん。ネットで調べたら、こっちより一ヶ月ぐらい遅く咲くって。
lines.kana: うん。ねっとでしらべたら、こっちよりいっかげつぐらいおそくさくって。
lines.english: Yeah. I looked it up online: they come out about a month later than here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, atchi de sakura ga saitara, asobi ni iku! kotoshi wa nikai mireru ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、あっちで桜が咲いたら、遊びに行く！今年は二回見れるね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あっちでさくらがさいたら、あそびにいく！ことしはにかいみれるね。
lines.english: Then when they come out up there, I'm coming to visit! I'll get to see them twice this year.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, kuru no? jaa, yuki ga tsumottara, tetsudai ni kite yo.
lines.ja: え、来るの？じゃあ、雪が積もったら、手伝いに来てよ。
lines.kana: え、くるの？じゃあ、ゆきがつもったら、てつだいにきてよ。
lines.english: Wait, you're coming? Then come and help me out when the snow piles up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa muri. watashi, samusa ni yowai kara.
lines.ja: それは無理。私、寒さに弱いから。
lines.kana: それはむり。わたし、さむさによわいから。
lines.english: No way. I can't take the cold.

questions.english: What does Yuki decide to do?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何を決めましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなにをきめましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nani o kimemashita ka?

choices.english: Go up in winter to help Kenji when the snow piles up.
Visit Kenji when the cherry blossoms come out up there, about a month after they come out at home.
Try to talk Kenji into a university nearer home, since he's no good in the cold either.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji is going to university in Hokkaido, partly because he can't take the heat. Lines 13-15: the cherry blossoms come out about a month later up there, so Yuki says she'll visit when they do (atchi de sakura ga saitara, asobi ni iku) and get to see them twice this year. A is wrong: Kenji asks her to come and help when the snow piles up (line 16), but she says no, because she can't take the cold herself (line 17). C is wrong: Yuki teases him about the cold (line 11), but she never tries to change his mind.

questions.english: It's early April. Kenji has moved to Hokkaido, where the cherry blossoms won't be out for weeks. He calls and asks, "sotchi, sakura dou?" (how are the blossoms there?). The ones near you are out. Tell him, using saku.
questions.answer: Say they're out with saiteru: mou saiteru yo (they're already out). Saita says they've come out, saiteru says they're out now, and mada saitenai is not out yet. Don't reach for deru: hana ga deru isn't said.

modelAnswers.romaji: mou saiteru yo. ima ga ichiban kirei.
modelAnswers.ja: もう咲いてるよ。今が一番きれい。
modelAnswers.english: They're already out. They're at their best right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: kinou saita yo. sotchi wa mada saitenai desho?
modelAnswers.ja: 昨日咲いたよ。そっちはまだ咲いてないでしょ？
modelAnswers.english: They came out yesterday. Yours aren't out yet, are they?

questions.explanation: Yuki and Kenji use saku for the blossoms in lines 13 to 15: atchi tte sakura ga saku no, osoi n da yo ne? (they come out late up there, don't they?), osoku saku tte (they come out later), and atchi de sakura ga saitara (when they come out up there). Flowers coming out is saku, and flowers that are out now are saiteru. English 'the blossoms are out' tempts deru, but hana ga deru isn't said, and hiraku (open) is for describing petals, not for chat. When the petals come down, it's chiru: mou chitchatta. In casual talk ga usually drops: sakura saita?

questions.english: It's a scorching day in August. Yuki suggests eating lunch outside: "ohiru, soto de tabenai?" Say no: you just can't take the heat. Use atsusa ni yowai.
questions.kana: おひる、そとでたべない？
questions.answer: Explain with atsusa ni yowai, often as atsusa ni yowai n da (the thing is, I'm no good in the heat). Keep the ni: atsusa ga yowai would mean the heat itself is weak.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, atsusa ni yowai n da. naka de tabenai?
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、暑さに弱いんだ。中で食べない？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I can't take the heat. Can we eat inside?

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto. atsusa ni yowai kara, naka ni shiyou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと。暑さに弱いから、中にしようよ。
modelAnswers.english: Not today. I'm no good in the heat, so let's eat inside.

questions.explanation: Kenji's reason for Hokkaido is atsusa ni yowai kara (line 2), Yuki agrees he always has been (line 3), and he sets it against the cold in line 10: atsusa ni wa yowai kedo, samusa ni wa yowakunai. Yuki turns it round on him at the end: samusa ni yowai kara (line 17). Yowai with ni means you can't handle something, like osake ni yowai (can't hold your drink), and with atsusa the ni stays, never ga. Atsusa and samusa are atsui and samui made into nouns with -sa. Atsui no nigate (I can't do heat) is just as everyday; the opposite is atsusa ni tsuyoi.

questions.english: Kenji complains about summers at home. What did he say about the cicadas?
questions.ja: ケンジはセミについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはせみについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa semi ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: the cicadas sing from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga utatte, nerarenai shi

choices.english: the cicadas ring from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga natte, nerarenai shi

choices.english: the cicadas call from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi

questions.explanation: Line 4: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. Insects, birds and animals all naku (鳴く), which sounds the same as naku 'cry' (泣く): semi ga naku, tori ga naku, neko ga naku. A carries the English verb over: utau is singing a song, and tori ga utau is poetry, not chat. B uses naru, which is for things that make a sound, like denwa ga naru or kaminari ga naru: animals naku, things naru. Yuki says it too (line 5: semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji), and Kenji again in line 6 (semi anmari nakanai).

questions.english: Yuki warns Kenji about winter in Hokkaido. What does she say about the snow?
questions.ja: 北海道の冬について、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ほっかいどうのふゆについて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: hokkaidou no fuyu ni tsuite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: A lot of it builds up, and once it's lying on the ground it's hard work.
It hardly ever falls there, but when it does, it's freezing.
It falls almost every day, but it's always gone by the next morning.

questions.explanation: Line 7: atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo (the snow really piles up there). Line 9: futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo (pretty while it's coming down, hard work once it settles). Furu is snow coming down; tsumoru is snow building up and staying, so yuki tsumotteru means there's snow on the ground. B is wrong: she says a lot of it piles up. C is wrong: snow that tsumoru stays put; snow melting is tokeru. Snow stuck on things, like a car, is tsuku: kuruma ni yuki ga tsuiteru.
